queries.text: Third-order connected (linked-cluster) contributions at the retained single plaquette: which words in the Hodge generators (up-Laplacian and the adjacency, non-Laplacian operator) of length at most three leave the plaquette state and return, with the rule that a return needs two adjacency insertions with no up-Laplacian between them, so words with the up-Laplacian in the middle factorize (disconnected) while words with the adjacency operator in the middle are connected

Rooted cumulant bookkeeping for generator words up to length three on the retained plaquette (carrier) state: excursion words are those where the non-Laplacian operator (adjacency, shared-link hopping) appears twice with no up-Laplacian in between; the word with the up-Laplacian in the middle factorizes into a product of shorter words while the one with the adjacency operator in the middle does not

Which length-three products of the plaquette Hodge Laplacian generators produce a leave-and-return (off-diagonal then back) amplitude on the retained plaquette state, and why the factorization rule separates adjacency-in-the-middle words from up-Laplacian-in-the-middle words

Cluster expansion of the moments of the plaquette Laplacian in the retained plaquette state: the diagonal up-Laplacian placed between two off-diagonal non-Laplacian insertions factorizes, whereas the adjacency operator between two insertions gives a genuinely connected word
